chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The woman is jealous of the man, causing him distress.' He said, 'That is from love.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a wife's jealousy in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contextualizes *ghayrah* (jealousy/sense of honor) not merely as possessiveness, but as an intrinsic indicator of deep affection (*hubb*) within the marital bond. This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that *ghayrah* is a virtue when it protects the sanctity of the relationship, distinguishing it from destructive envy, and serves as a spiritual metric for the sincerity of love between spouses.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The woman expresses jealousy upon the man so she hurts him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is from the love’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
When a woman feels jealous against man, she causes disappointment for him.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because of (her) love/”
